In the latter case there could be a more severe but local impact on any biota, as well as the addition of particulate matter. The shock wave would have negligible effects on sediments and bedrock, except in the uppermost water-saturated and unconsolidated sediment which may be locally displaced and the contained biota damaged.
16. Thermal Effects. The access hole through the ice shelf will be maintained open with a thermal cable; minimum melting of the snow-firn-ice strata will result during the period of the project. The temperature in the upwelled seawater will be maintained near the seawater temperature to preserve the integrity of the biological specimens. This will involve heat transference to the ice adjacent to the access hole in order to lower the rate of freeze-back to an acceptable level. The alteration of the snow, firn and ice will be negligible over a long time period because, on retrieval of the thermal cable, the water in the hole will freeze leaving a column of salty ice, and the temperature of the surrounding ice will drop until the regional temperature gradient is reestablished.
17. <u>Inadvertent Hardware Loss</u>. Solid, non-combustible wastes collected from the camp and operation sites will be back-loaded to McMurdo Station (see 7 above). However, artifacts of the working operation, including metal stripping, tools, etc., can be expected to escape recovery from time to time.
